prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1104; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle and a second car, with the claimant reporting a knee injury and retaining counsel before the file was opened.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver listed as the insured is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time reported.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene, though no independent witness statements or photographs of the collision have been located to date.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle damage estimate; the crush pattern and point of contact are consistent with the impact described in the first notice.

Entry 5: Claimant's account was taken by phone and repeated again in a second conversation with counsel present, with the sequence of events matching in each telling.

Entry 6: Medical records show a knee injury whose type and severity fit the force expected from a side impact of this kind, and no prior treatment to that body area has turned up in the records requested.

Entry 7: Noted a few old scratches on the vehicle that may predate this collision; the photos will be reviewed to separate them from new damage.

Entry 8: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this type of knee injury, and the treating provider's notes have been requested to understand the reasons for the extended course.

Entry 9: Checked policy history and found nothing indicating the damage occurred before coverage began; the effective dates remain consistent with the loss.

Entry 10: Counsel has been asked for the claimant's full treatment list and any additional documents supporting the injury claim; the file remains open pending receipt.

Entry 11: Reviewed the file summary with the supervisor, who agreed that the outstanding items are the provider notes, the full scratch photo set, and independent confirmation of the collision if any becomes available.
